Scoring recomputed by hand against as_of 2026-10-20: Fed hawkish base 22 / eff 15.5 (fed-h2 34d x0.25; h1,h3 x0.5; h4,h5,h8 x0.75; h6,h7 x1), dovish base 17 / eff 12.5 -> base +5, effective +3.0, band 'lean hike' (follows base as publish.py enforces; effective +3.0 sits on the hold boundary and FedWatch prices ~83% hold - divergence surfaced, not an error). BoC hawkish base 17 / eff 12.5, dovish base 9 / eff 7.0 -> base +8, effective +5.5, band 'strong hike lean' - matches. Mean |weight| Fed 2.79, BoC 2.89; no weight >=5; one same-URL split (boc-h6 headline-energy vs boc-d4 core-cooling, StatCan dq261019a) has distinct facets and separate transmission chains. Implied rates: Fed 3.875 + 0.172x0.25 = 3.918 -> 3.92 (prior-round rounding slip now resolved); BoC 2.25 + 0.78x0.25 = 2.445 -> 2.45. Prior round (2026-10-19, 7 next_cycle minors): fed-h1 previous (revised Jul 3.4/3.0), fed-h2 source_url (fomcprojtabl20260916), boc-h5 'significantly' attribution and Fed implied_rate_after are fixed; the BOS calendar row is moot (event passed, row removed); fed-h4 market_validation and the fed-d3 Williams/Reuters overlap are only partially addressed and carried again (minors). Facts verified via WebSearch (direct fetch of statcan/bankofcanada/cmegroup/polymarket blocked by network policy, so primary pages were corroborated through indexed copies and wire coverage): Sep CPI 3.1% vs 3.2% consensus, gasoline +27.8% (Aug +22.8%), ex-gasoline 2.2% from 2.4%, CPI-trim 1.8% from 1.9%, CPI-median 1.9% from 2.0% (Reuters/US News, briefs.co, wowa.ca, ActionForex headline); Q3 BOS indicator -0.33 vs -0.38 (investinglive; Q2 later revised -0.39), 'roughly half of firms, more than in the previous quarter' plan to pass on war/tariff costs (Bank of Canada BOS Q3 2026 text), ~three-quarters of interviews before the trade-talk breakdown (The Hub/CP), CSCE 5y expectations up (~3.91% vs 3.39%); BMO, RBC (securities unit) and Desjardins flipped to an Oct 28 hike to 2.50% on Oct 19 (Bloomberg via CMT News); BBH Oct 20 'swaps pricing a 78% probability' of +25bp and '100 bps of tightening priced over the next year as excessive' (FXStreet 202610201438) - BoC pricing confirmed; corroborating range ~80% (Bloomberg, late Oct 19) to ~85% (LSEG/Reuters, early Oct 20), Commerzbank '36% to more than 75%'. Fed: CME FedWatch ~80% hold on Oct 19 (Forbes) is consistent with 82.8/17.2 on Oct 20, Dec hike firmly expected; Polymarket October hold 86 / hike 14 (KuCoin flash) consistent with the filed 85/15; Brent Dec settled $108.79 after a $111.99 high on Oct 20 (CNBC); UMich Oct prelim 46.3, 1y 4.7%, 5y 3.5%, final due Oct 23 (investinglive/advisorperspectives); BEA Q3 GDP advance + Sep Personal Income & Outlays both Oct 29 08:30 (bea.gov schedule); StatCan Aug retail advance estimate +1.3% and Jul -0.7% (CP/BNN). Not independently verifiable here: exact 82.8/17.2 FedWatch print, the '87% by 2:45pm' Bloomberg/CMT figure (indexed coverage shows ~80-85%), Polymarket volume $49.9M and the stale BoC Polymarket 67/33 (correctly labelled stale), CPI m/m +0.1% NSA/+0.4% SA and the +0.2% m/m consensus, RBC's 3.7%/3.1% firm-expectation read, the Oct 23 08:30 retail-sales timestamp and ex-autos +1.0% consensus. None of these changes the hold/hike call or a band; they are noted as minors or left as labelled. Blocking issue (1 major): boc-h6 reason states September 'pushed the headline out of the 1-3% control range for the first time this cycle' - false: May 2026 CPI printed 3.2% y/y (released Jun 22) and Reuters describes September as above the upper limit 'once again after three months'. A wrong claim stated as fact in a scored driver - drivers check fails. Verdict: REVISE. Operator: rewrite the boc-h6 reason (e.g., 'back above the 1-3% range for the first time since May'), re-run check + freeze, and resubmit; the scoring, pricing and calendar otherwise reproduce and the minors below can ride to the next cycle.

findings.issue: Reason claims the Sep CPI 'pushed the headline out of the 1-3% control range for the first time this cycle'. That is false: headline CPI was 3.2% y/y in May 2026, already above the band, so September is a re-breach after three months inside it. The wrong framing makes the breach look novel and overstates the hawkish signal.

May 2026 CPI 3.2% y/y vs 2.8% Apr, released 2026-06-22 (wealthprofessional.ca/news/industry-news/canadas-may-inflation-rate-revealed/392789; metalsmine.com/news/1404744-canada-consumer-price-index-may-2026; babypips 'headline-canada-cpi-may-2026'); Reuters/Yahoo 2026-10-19 'Inflation rises to 3.1% in September': CPI 'above the Bank of Canada's upper limit once again after three months'.

findings.issue: Carried from 2026-10-19 and only partly fixed. Facets now split fed-h3 ('inflation-level') from fed-d3 ('october-timing'), but fed-d3 still restates Williams' 'no urgency', which fed-d1 already scores at -3 (both drivers are about October timing). It is also a Reuters retelling scored at the same weight as primary-source drivers and used as its own market_validation. Merging the Williams part would make the Fed total more hawkish (base +5 -> about +6..+8), so this is no longer neutral to the band. This is the second round; escalate to major if it is still unfixed next cycle.

findings.issue: Carried from 2026-10-19 and only partly fixed. The CPI-day move was replaced with an Oct 12 level ('~18% after the release'), but the Oct 12 reading is five days after the Oct 7 minutes, after Waller and the payroll repricing, and it is a level, not a move caused by the minutes. The same '~18% Oct 12 (CME FedWatch)' reading is also used to validate the dovish fed-d3, so one number supports both sides. Use an Oct 7-8 move or set it to 'unverified'.

findings.issue: The headline facts check out (about half of firms, more than in Q2, plan to pass costs through; indicator -0.33 vs -0.38; consumers' 5y expectations up; BMO, RBC and Desjardins flipped). But the data block lists only the hawkish parts of a survey whose overall sentiment improved (future-sales balance +42 vs +15; firms expecting a recession 6% vs 17%). The '87% by 2:45pm' and the RBC '3.7% 1y / 3.1% 2y' firm-expectation read could not be corroborated: indexed coverage shows about 80% (Bloomberg, late Oct 19) to about 85% (LSEG/Reuters, early Oct 20). Add the offsetting survey readings and label the 87% as a single secondary print.

findings.issue: surprise=1 is not supported by any evidence: data.forecast is 'unverified', and a pre-release preview (RBC) expected core to ease to about 1.8%. Without a consensus, the 'surprise' point is unsupported. Removing it would make boc-d4 a 2 and move the BoC base from +8 to +9 (band unchanged), so the effect is cosmetic, but every breakdown part needs evidence.
